title: Systemic Site/Scene Variant, Template & Promotion Integration
objective: Integrate PCA-02/PCA-03 procedural candidates with stable canonical site/location identity, owner-backed current/historical/alternate variants, presentation handoffs, explicit ephemeral/proposed/persistent state, GM/owner-authorized promotion receipts, and versioned transformation Campaign templates without allowing generated content to become Campaign truth merely because generation succeeded.
acceptance: Systemic site/scene candidates consume exact PCA-02/PCA-03 recipe/seed/cache references without MSWI recreating generic procedural infrastructure.
Stable canonical location/site identity remains unchanged across current, historical and alternate variants.
Variant selection is derived only from accepted owner state and exact versions; missing owner facts remain unresolved rather than inferred.
MCS, MAS, MSAS, MCCS and ARI presentation handoffs reference accepted presentation owners without transferring canonical location/world authority.
Ephemeral, proposed and persistent states remain distinct; generation success alone never promotes a candidate to Campaign truth.
Promotion requires explicit GM/owner authorization and produces an attributable promotion receipt against exact candidate and owner versions.
Transformation Campaign templates bind/version accepted MSWI primitives and MRCS-authored definitions without forking the runtime or creating genre authority.
Permission filtering precedes variant counts, search, diagnostics, explanation, AI context and export.
Blocking workflows remain deterministic/provider-off, semantic/textual, keyboard-capable, optional-AI independent and paid-cloud independent.
boundaries: MSWI-01, MSWI-03, MSWI-04, MSWI-06 and MSWI-07 plus all upstream completed programs remain sealed.
PCA-02/PCA-03 retain generic recipe/DAG/seed/cache infrastructure authority; MSWI-14 owns only systemic adapters and promotion integration.

MCS retains canonical map/cartographic geometry authority, MAS retains scene/site assembly authority, MCCS presentation authority, MSAS/AAI audio authority and ARI its governed presentation/runtime authority.
Generated or proposed content remains non-canonical until explicit GM/owner promotion succeeds.
Stable site/location identity is not replaced by a variant or template.
Transformation Campaign templates configure accepted primitives and definitions; they do not fork MSWI runtime behavior or create genre canon.
MSWI-18 remains unauthorized until canonical MSWI-14 closeout.
